article: Empirically speaking
stem: A chief compliance officer encounters an organization with overlapping compliance responsibilities and inconsistent control ownership. What is the MOST appropriate next step?
options: Map the workflow, clarify accountable owners and handoffs, then test the controls against real cases.
Map the workflow, clarify accountable owners and handoffs, but defer testing the controls against real cases until after management considers the matter closed.
Assign every control to compliance irrespective of operational ownership.
Introduce a new tool before identifying the source of process failure.
explanation: The best choice is to map the workflow, clarify accountable owners and handoffs, then test the controls against real cases. This approach focuses on program design rather than relying on an untested shortcut. The other options either substitute assertions for evidence, postpone assessment, or weaken accountability. Editorial basis: CEP 2024-12, Empirically speaking, p. 13; verify the precise article passage before using this in a scored mock exam.

Conclude controls are effective because employees completed their attestations.
Reduce monitoring until regulators identify a formal violation.
